name: markov_model
description: A state-transition (Markov) diagram: 2–6 health/process states as circles, transition arrows between them (with a probability/rate label), and self-loops for states that also "stay" (optionally captioned with the stay probability). Choose this for ANY request about a Markov model, a health-state transition diagram, or a cycle of states with probabilities of moving between them. All placement is computed for you: a ring for 3+ states or a horizontal row (layout "chain" — the classic textbook style for health-state models), self-loops aimed into each state's least crowded side, and arrows that bow around any state that sits in their way. A state that no transition ever leaves renders as absorbing (plain ink, no color) automatically.

states.description: 2–6 state names, in the order they should be laid out.

transitions.description: Directed transitions between states named in `states`.

self_loops.description: States that also have a "stay" probability — drawn with a small loop aimed into the state's least crowded side. A bare state name, or {state, label} to caption the stay probability.

layout.description: Node arrangement. Default: circle for 3+ states, chain for exactly 2. Pick "chain" explicitly for the classic left-to-right row (e.g. Well → Sick → Dead) — skip-ahead transitions arc around the states between them.

highlight_state.description: One state name (must be in `states`) to highlight with a tinted halo behind it.

element_ids.state_<slug>: the ellipse for one state (slug: the state name, lowercased, non-alphanumeric characters replaced with _)
element_ids.state_label_<slug>: the state's name, centered inside its ellipse
element_ids.t_<i>: transition arrow i (0-indexed, in `transitions` order) — bowed automatically when the reverse transition also exists, or to arc around a state that sits in its way
element_ids.t_label_<i>: transition i's probability/rate label, when set
element_ids.loop_<slug>: the self-loop for a state named in `self_loops`
element_ids.loop_label_<slug>: that loop's stay-probability caption, when its `self_loops` entry set a label
element_ids.hl_<slug>: tinted halo behind the state named by `highlight_state` — present only when set
element_ids.title: figure title, when set

examples.request: Draw a three-state Markov model: Well, Sick, Dead, with Well and Sick able to stay or transition, and Dead absorbing.
Draw the classic Well–Sick–Dead Markov model as a left-to-right row, with stay probabilities on Well and Sick and a direct Well-to-Dead arrow.
Draw a two-state Markov chain for a machine that's either working or broken, with a repair rate and a breakdown rate.
